samples.scenario: Prediction target period: from 2023-10-29 to 2024-01-14. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Following promising phase 1 results, a global phase 2 clinical trial (NCT05968326) to evaluate a personalized mRNA-based cancer vaccine for surgically removed pancreatic cancer began on October 18, 2023. The trial is sponsored by Genentech, a member of the Roche Group, in collaboration with BioNTech. It will assess the efficacy and safety of the individualized immunotherapy autogene cevumeran (also known as BNT122 or RO7198457) combined with the checkpoint inhibitor atezolizumab and standard chemotherapy (mFOLFIRINOX), compared to chemotherapy alone. The open-label, randomized trial aims to enroll approximately 260 patients with resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) across sites in the United States, Europe, and the Asia Pacific region, including Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. [6, 8, 9] The first patient's treatment was formally announced in a press release on October 19, 2023. [6] The primary goal is to determine if the vaccine combination improves disease-free survival. [6] <2> On October 16, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved pembrolizumab (Keytruda) for the treatment of resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). The approval specifies a perioperative regimen where pembrolizumab is used in combination with platinum-containing chemotherapy as a neoadjuvant (pre-surgical) treatment, followed by its use as a single agent for adjuvant (post-surgical) therapy. This indication is for patients with resectable NSCLC whose tumors are at least 4 cm or are node-positive. The approval was based on the results of the KEYNOTE-671 phase 3 trial, a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study involving 797 patients. The trial demonstrated that the pembrolizumab regimen led to statistically significant improvements in both event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS) compared to a placebo and chemotherapy regimen. <3> On October 13, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved nivolumab (Opdivo) for the adjuvant treatment of adult and pediatric patients aged 12 years and older with completely resected Stage IIB or Stage IIC melanoma. [1, 2] This approval was based on the results of the phase 3 CheckMate-76K trial, which demonstrated that nivolumab significantly reduced the risk of recurrence-free survival compared to a placebo. [1, 6] In the trial, which enrolled 790 patients, nivolumab lowered the risk of disease recurrence, new primary melanoma, or death by 58%. [6] The one-year recurrence-free survival rate was 89% for patients treated with nivolumab, compared to 79% for those who received the placebo. [6] <4> On October 11, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved the combination of encorafenib (Braftovi) and binimetinib (Mektovi) for the treatment of adult patients with metastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) harboring a BRAF V600E mutation. [1, 2, 3, 4] This approval was based on findings from the phase 2 PHAROS trial. [2, 4] The FDA also approved the FoundationOne CDx (tissue) and FoundationOne Liquid CDx (plasma) tests as companion diagnostics to detect the specific mutation. [1, 6, 7] <5> Between July and September 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved several new cancer therapies, enriching the treatment landscape for various malignancies. Key approvals during this period include treatments for multiple myeloma, prostate cancer with BRCA mutations, acute myeloid leukemia (AML), and endometrial cancer. Specifically for multiple myeloma, approvals included motixafortide (Aphexda) on September 11, 2023, to help in mobilizing hematopoietic stem cells for transplantation. Additionally, in August, the FDA granted accelerated approvals to two bispecific antibodies for heavily pretreated relapsed or refractory multiple myeloma: talquetamab-tgvs (Talvey) on August 9, 2023 and elranatamab-bcmm (Elrexfio) on August 14, 2023. For prostate cancer, the FDA approved a fixed-dose combination of niraparib and abiraterone acetate (Akeega) with prednisone on August 11, 2023. This therapy is for patients with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) who have deleterious or suspected deleterious BRCA mutations. Other notable approvals in this timeframe include quizartinib (Vanflyta) on July 20, 2023, for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) that is FLT3-ITD-positive. On July 31, 2023, dostarlimab-gxly (Jemperli) in combination with chemotherapy was approved for primary advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer that is mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H). Furthermore, on August 9, 2023, pralsetinib (Gavreto) received regular approval for metastatic RET fusion-positive non-small cell lung cancer. A therapy for liver metastases from uveal melanoma was not approved within this timeframe; tebentafusp-tebn (Kimmtrak) was approved for unresectable or metastatic uveal melanoma on January 25, 2022. <6> On September 26, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved bosutinib (Bosulif) for pediatric patients aged one year and older. The approval covers the treatment of chronic phase (CP), Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph+) chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML) that is either newly diagnosed or has proven resistant or intolerant to previous therapies. The FDA also approved new 50 mg and 100 mg capsule dosage forms. This approval was based on the results of the BCHILD clinical trial, a multicenter, open-label study. <7> A study published in the journal Cancer on behalf of the National Cancer Institute (NCI) presented findings from the "Annual Report to the Nation on the Status of Cancer, Part 2," which focused on the initial impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on cancer diagnoses. The report revealed a sharp decline in new diagnoses for six major cancer types—breast, colorectal, lung, pancreatic, prostate, and thyroid—between March and May 2020. This drop coincided with a steep decrease in the volume of pathology reports, suggesting that interruptions to healthcare services and fewer screenings led to many cancers going undiagnosed. Researchers expressed concern that these missed or delayed diagnoses could lead to worse outcomes in the future. By July 2020, new diagnoses for most of the studied cancers, with the exception of prostate cancer, had returned to pre-pandemic levels. <8> From September 17-20, 2023, nearly 700 cancer patients, survivors, and advocates representing all 50 states, Washington, D.C., Guam, and Puerto Rico convened in Washington, D.C. for the American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network's (ACS CAN) annual Leadership Summit and Lobby Day. [1] The multi-day event, now in its third decade, involved training sessions and culminated in advocates meeting with members of Congress. [1] Their primary goal was to urge lawmakers to designate cancer as a national priority and to secure increased federal funding for cancer research and prevention programs ahead of the 2024 budget deadline. [1] Specifically, advocates lobbied for $51 billion for the National Institutes of Health (NIH), which included $9.98 billion for the National Cancer Institute, and for increased funding for CDC cancer programs. [1] <9> On September 13, 2023, the American Association for Cancer Research (AACR) announced the formation of the AACR Cancer Centers Alliance, a new initiative to promote collaboration and leverage resources among the nation's cancer centers. [1, 7] The announcement coincided with a briefing in Washington, D.C., and the publication of an article detailing the Alliance's mission in the AACR journal, Cancer Discovery. [1, 7] This initiative, described as an unprecedented partnership, aims to unite cancer centers to expand their collective impact for the benefit of all patients. [1, 2] The Alliance was formed after a series of meetings over the preceding year where cancer center directors concluded they could have a greater impact by working together. [1, 7] Key goals include enhancing federally funded cancer research programs, developing innovative funding models, sharing best practices and core facilities, improving clinical trials, and speaking with a unified voice on science and health policy. [1, 3] The initiative also aligns with the objectives of the national Cancer Moonshot to reduce cancer mortality. [1, 4] <10> The 'Fairness to Kids with Cancer Act of 2023,' designated as H.R.5405, was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives on September 12, 2023. [1, 5, 7, 10] The bill, sponsored by Rep. Brian K. Fitzpatrick [R-PA-1], proposes that the percentage of federal funds for cancer research allocated to pediatric cancer research must be equal to the percentage of the U.S. population under the age of 18. [2, 7, 10] Following its introduction, the bill was referred to the Subcommittee on Health on September 15, 2023. [7, 10]

samples.scenario: Prediction target period: from 2023-11-26 to 2024-02-11. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On November 16, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved capivasertib (Truqap) in combination with fulvestrant. This treatment is for adult patients with hormone receptor (HR)-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has one or more PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN alterations. The therapy is indicated for patients whose cancer progressed after at least one endocrine-based regimen in the metastatic setting or who had a recurrence on or within 12 months of completing adjuvant therapy. The FDA also approved the FoundationOne®CDx assay to be used as a companion diagnostic to identify eligible patients. <2> On November 15, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved repotrectinib (brand name Augtyro) for the treatment of adult patients with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). This approval, announced by Bristol Myers Squibb on the same day, provides a new therapeutic option for both tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI)-naïve patients and those who have been previously treated with a ROS1 inhibitor. The approval was based on the results of the pivotal Phase 1/2 TRIDENT-1 clinical trial. Augtyro is the first and only next-generation TKI approved that includes patients previously treated with a ROS1 TKI. <3> On November 8, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved fruquintinib (Fruzaqla) for adult patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). The approval is for patients who have previously been treated with standard therapies, including fluoropyrimidine-, oxaliplatin-, and irinotecan-based chemotherapy, an anti-VEGF therapy, and if RAS wild-type, an anti-EGFR therapy. Developed by Takeda Pharmaceuticals, Fruzaqla is a highly selective oral inhibitor of VEGFR-1, -2, and -3. It is the first novel, chemotherapy-free targeted treatment approved in the United States in over a decade for this patient population, regardless of biomarker status, addressing a significant need for new options. <4> At the Society for Immunotherapy of Cancer (SITC) 38th Annual Meeting in November 2023, researchers presented updated interim results from the ARTACUS clinical trial. The findings, delivered in an oral presentation, showed that the oncolytic immunotherapy RP1 demonstrated significant anti-tumor activity in solid organ transplant recipients with advanced skin cancers. Specifically, RP1 monotherapy resulted in an overall response rate of 34.8% in 23 evaluable patients, with most responses ongoing as of the September 18, 2023 data cutoff. The trial is significant because this patient population has limited treatment options, as they are often ineligible for standard immunotherapies due to the risk of organ rejection from their chronic immunosuppressive treatment. The study found no evidence of allograft rejection and the safety profile was similar to that in non-immunocompromised patients. <5> Researchers at the National Cancer Institute (NCI) have engineered a promising new approach to bolster T-cell based immunotherapies against solid tumors. Their method, detailed in a study published in *Clinical Cancer Research*, involves modifying T-cells to carry two specific cytokines, IL-15 and IL-21, on their surface. This technique is designed to provide a targeted boost to the T-cells' cancer-fighting capabilities directly at the tumor site, potentially reducing the severe side effects associated with systemically administering large amounts of cytokines. In preclinical mouse models of cervical cancer and pediatric neuroblastoma, these dual-cytokine T-cells demonstrated a significantly enhanced ability to shrink tumors compared to T-cells with only one or no cytokines. Specifically, in the cervical cancer model, the enhanced T-cells led to complete tumor regression in 80% of the mice. This innovative strategy holds the potential to improve the effectiveness of treatments like CAR T-cell therapy for solid tumors, which have historically been difficult to treat with this type of immunotherapy. Researchers are continuing to evaluate this approach in further preclinical studies with the aim of advancing to human clinical trials. <6> The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved pembrolizumab (Keytruda) in combination with the chemotherapy drugs gemcitabine and cisplatin for the treatment of locally advanced unresectable or metastatic biliary tract cancer (BTC). [1, 4, 5] This approval was based on the results of the KEYNOTE-966, a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial involving 1,069 patients with BTC who had not previously received systemic therapy for advanced disease. [1, 2] The trial demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in overall survival (OS) for patients receiving pembrolizumab with chemotherapy compared to those receiving a placebo with chemotherapy. [2] The median OS was 12.7 months in the pembrolizumab group versus 10.9 months in the placebo group. [2, 3] Common adverse reactions leading to the interruption of treatment included decreased neutrophil and platelet counts, anemia, and fatigue. [1] <7> On October 27, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved toripalimab-tpzi (Loqtorzi) for the treatment of nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). This approval encompasses two indications: as a first-line treatment in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine for adults with metastatic or recurrent locally advanced NPC, and as a monotherapy for adults with recurrent, unresectable, or metastatic NPC whose disease has progressed during or after treatment with platinum-containing chemotherapy. The approval of Loqtorzi, a next-generation PD-1 monoclonal antibody, was based on the positive results from the JUPITER-02 Phase 3 study and the POLARIS-02 Phase 2 study. In the JUPITER-02 trial, toripalimab combined with chemotherapy reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 48% and the risk of death by 37% compared to chemotherapy alone. The POLARIS-02 study demonstrated durable antitumor activity for Loqtorzi as a single agent in patients who had previously received chemotherapy. Developed by Coherus BioSciences, Inc., and Shanghai Junshi Biosciences Co., Ltd., Loqtorzi is the first FDA-approved treatment for NPC. <8> On October 24, 2023, President Joe Biden awarded Dr. Steven A. Rosenberg, the Chief of the Surgery Branch at the National Cancer Institute (NCI), the National Medal of Technology and Innovation during a ceremony in the East Room of the White House. [1, 2, 3] This award is the United States' highest honor for technological achievement. [2, 3] Dr. Rosenberg, a pioneer in immunotherapy, was recognized for his transformative work in developing the first effective immunotherapies, which have significantly advanced cancer treatment and saved numerous lives. [1, 4, 5] <9> The primary results of the DESTINY-PanTumor02 Phase II trial, published in the Journal of Clinical Oncology, demonstrated the efficacy and safety of trastuzumab deruxtecan (Enhertu) in patients with various pre-treated, HER2-expressing solid tumors. [1] The study, a global, open-label trial, included 267 patients across seven cohorts: biliary tract, bladder, cervical, endometrial, ovarian, pancreatic, and other tumors. [5, 6] As of the data cutoff on June 8, 2023, with a median follow-up of 12.75 months, the overall patient population showed a confirmed objective response rate (ORR) of 37.1%, a median duration of response (DOR) of 11.3 months, a median progression-free survival (PFS) of 6.9 months, and a median overall survival (OS) of 13.4 months. [6, 8] Notably, patients with the highest level of HER2 expression (IHC 3+) experienced the greatest benefit, with a confirmed ORR of 61.3%, a median DOR of 22.1 months, a median PFS of 11.9 months, and a median OS of 21.1 months. [5, 8] The safety profile was consistent with previous findings, with adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease/pneumonitis occurring in 10.5% of patients, including three fatalities. [6] These results, which were also presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) 2023 Congress, suggest that trastuzumab deruxtecan could be a potential tumor-agnostic therapy for this patient population. [8] <10> Following promising phase 1 results, a global phase 2 clinical trial (NCT05968326) to evaluate a personalized mRNA-based cancer vaccine for surgically removed pancreatic cancer began on October 18, 2023. The trial is sponsored by Genentech, a member of the Roche Group, in collaboration with BioNTech. It will assess the efficacy and safety of the individualized immunotherapy autogene cevumeran (also known as BNT122 or RO7198457) combined with the checkpoint inhibitor atezolizumab and standard chemotherapy (mFOLFIRINOX), compared to chemotherapy alone. The open-label, randomized trial aims to enroll approximately 260 patients with resected pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) across sites in the United States, Europe, and the Asia Pacific region, including Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center. [6, 8, 9] The first patient's treatment was formally announced in a press release on October 19, 2023. [6] The primary goal is to determine if the vaccine combination improves disease-free survival. [6]

Developed by Takeda Pharmaceuticals, Fruzaqla is a highly selective oral inhibitor of VEGFR-1, -2, and -3. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On March 7, 2024, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted accelerated approval for the combination of zanubrutinib (Brukinsa) and obinutuzumab (Gazyva) to treat adult patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) follicular lymphoma (FL). This approval is for patients who have already undergone two or more prior lines of systemic therapy. The approval was based on the results of the phase 2 ROSEWOOD trial, which showed that the combination therapy resulted in a higher overall response rate (69%) compared to obinutuzumab alone (46%). With a median follow-up of about 19 months, the median duration of response had not been reached in the combination arm, while it was 14 months for the obinutuzumab monotherapy arm. This is the fifth approved indication for zanubrutinib, a BTK inhibitor from BeiGene, and the first time a BTK inhibitor has been approved for follicular lymphoma. <2> On March 6, 2024, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved nivolumab (Opdivo) in combination with cisplatin and gemcitabine for the first-line treatment of adult patients with unresectable or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (UC). This approval, which expands nivolumab's use to a first-line setting for this patient group, was based on the results of the Phase 3 CheckMate-901 trial. The trial demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in overall survival and progression-free survival for patients treated with the nivolumab combination compared to those who received cisplatin and gemcitabine alone. With a median follow-up of approximately 33 months, the nivolumab regimen reduced the risk of death by 22%, showing a median overall survival of 21.7 months versus 18.9 months for the chemotherapy-only group. <3> On March 6, 2024, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted full approval to inotuzumab ozogamicin (Besponsa), an antibody-drug conjugate manufactured by Pfizer, for the treatment of pediatric patients aged one year and older with relapsed or refractory CD22-positive B-cell precursor acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL). This approval addresses a significant need for new therapeutic options for this hard-to-treat pediatric blood cancer. The decision was based on a multicenter, single-arm, open-label study involving 53 pediatric patients which found that 42% of patients achieved complete remission. The application was granted Priority Review and Orphan Drug designation by the FDA. <4> On March 6, 2024, Cancer Grand Challenges, a global funding initiative co-founded by the National Cancer Institute (NCI) and Cancer Research UK, announced its largest investment to date: $125 million awarded to five new international research teams. [2, 3] The announcement was made at the Cancer Grand Challenges Summit in London. [1] Each team will receive up to $25 million over five years to tackle four of the most complex challenges in cancer research. [1, 2, 3] The selected teams and their challenges are: - **Solid Tumors in Children:** Two teams, KOODAC and PROTECT, will address this challenge. [3, 8] They aim to develop new therapies, such as protein degraders, to target the previously 'undruggable' drivers of these cancers. [4, 6] - **Cancer Inequities:** Team SAMBAI will build a comprehensive resource to understand the social, environmental, and biological factors causing disparities in cancer outcomes, focusing on prostate, breast, and pancreatic cancers in the global African diaspora. [1, 3] - **Early-Onset Cancers:** Team PROSPECT will investigate the rising incidence of cancers in adults under 50, with a specific focus on colorectal cancer. [1, 15] - **T-Cell Receptors:** Team MATCHMAKERS will work to decipher how T-cells recognize and target cancer cells to improve personalized immunotherapies. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> On October 8, 2025, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approved cemiplimab-rwlc (Libtayo) for the adjuvant treatment of adult patients with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (CSCC) at high risk of recurrence following surgery and radiation. This approval makes cemiplimab the first and only immunotherapy for this indication. The decision was based on the phase 3 C-POST trial (NCT03969004), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study involving 415 patients.
